analysis: Only docs/developer/test.md changed (head text lines 1-871 supplied; no patch). It is developer test documentation, with no runtime code, auth, attestation, encryption, billing, or availability behavior altered. Its content describes the synthetic App Attest endpoint-resumption and logout tests (lines 5-22), the native serving qualification harness (24-74), and ServeLoopAppAttest dispatch tests (76-93). It also covers the Autopilot rewards and cohort test commands and the SSD cache tests that relate to T-041. Security-relevant statements in the doc are protective: tests never contact Apple or live coordinators; DATABASE_URL must never be a production DSN; the harness uses an ephemeral SE signer and in-memory key IDs; the passive observation.json excludes request content, keys and proofs; the 0600/0700 diagnostic inputs; DARKBLOOM_SSD_TEST_TMPDIR is test-only and does not change the production cache root or disk reserve; and tests do not stop operator processes. The doc repeatedly disclaims that these tests do not establish native Apple qualification, production rollout or hardware attestation. I found no overclaims that contradict the threat model: T-052..T-058 assumptions are untouched, and T-041 (SSD at-rest posture, 30-min TTL, 20 GiB reserve) is consistent with what the doc describes. No threat-model update is needed beyond the docs-only change. Nothing was supplied for the referenced test sources or scripts, so the accuracy of the doc against them is a coverage limit rather than evidence of safety.
